# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: DECSTR soft terminal reset (CSI ! p)  (issue #80, wave 5)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/decstr_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output)
#
# Same machine-readable layout as csi_spec.txt (### ID / size / step / cite / note /
# screen / cursor / pending_wrap / requests / scrollback), parsed by tests/spec/mod.rs
# `parse_fixture`-style code. Extra keys the shared parser ignores and tests/decstr.rs
# must assert by hand because render_screen cannot show them:
#     pen:     expected Terminal::grid().pen() after the whole script ("default" = Style::DEFAULT)
#     cellpen: style of one printed cell, "(row,col)=default|<desc>"
#     region:  expected grid.scroll_region(): "full" or "top..=bottom" 0-based
#     tabs:    note only
#     flags:   xterm-quirk | decision | control | negative
# `control` cases run WITHOUT DECSTR and prove the setup really produces the state the
# neighbouring case claims to reset (guards against vacuous tests). `negative` cases send
# a sequence that looks like DECSTR but must not reach it. Every other case sends DECSTR;
# tests/decstr.rs checks that.
#     correction: a change the implementer made after running the hand-derived row (#80).
# Cursor is 0-based (row,col). render_screen puts `|` AFTER the cursor's cell; a row ending
# in `\` is soft-wrapped. `set auto_wrap|insert_mode true|false` is the Terminal seam.
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES (all read in full for this fixture)
#   [CTL]  xterm ctlseqs  https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html
#          "CSI ! p  Soft terminal reset (DECSTR), VT220 and up."  One line only: ctlseqs has NO
#          table of what DECSTR resets. The brief's "table in ctlseqs" does not exist.
#   [DEC]  VT510/VT520 RM  https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECSTR.html  Table 5-9
#          "Terminal's Default Settings" = the state after DECSTR (list in the header notes below).
#          DEC STD 070 is not online; xterm's comments cite its pages 5-186..5-191 (DECSC/DECRC),
#          D-19/D-20 (DECALN) and 14-9 (DECSASD on DECSTR).
#   [XT]   xterm source (the oracle), ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots master:
#            charproc.c CASE_DECSTR -> VTReset(xw, False, False) -> ReallyReset(xw, full=False, saved=False)
#            charproc.c ReallyReset() ~L14358..L14560 (common part, then `else { /* DECSTR */ }`)
#            charproc.c resetMarginMode(), resetCharsets(), reset_SGR_Colors()
#            cursor.c   CursorSave2() / CursorRestoreFlags()
#          DECSCL (`CSI 6x ; Ps " p`) also calls ReallyReset(soft): charproc.c CASE_DECSCL.
#   [KT]   kitty   kitty/vt-parser.c (`case '!': // Soft reset` -> screen_soft_reset, rejects params)
#                  kitty/screen.c do_screen_reset(self, is_hard_reset=false)
#   [WZ]   WezTerm term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs `Device::SoftReset` ("xterm deviates from the
#          documented DECSTR setting for dec_auto_wrap, so we do too")
#
# WHAT XTERM ACTUALLY DOES (ReallyReset, full=False) -- the authoritative reset list
#   common to soft and hard:  cursor visible; scroll region = full + DECLRMM off (resetMarginMode);
#     DECOM off; SGR colours reset (reset_SGR_Colors); G0-G3/GL/GR default (resetCharsets);
#     DECCKM, KAM, DECKPAM cleared (then resource default); modifyOtherKeys back to resource;
#     DECSCA (protected) off; DECSASD main display.
#   soft only:  WRAPAROUND/REVERSEWRAP/REVERSEWRAP2 := resource default (autoWrap resource = True, so ON);
#     flags INSERT INVERSE BOLD BLINK UNDERLINE INVISIBLE cleared; ResetItalics;
#     CursorSave(xw) -- saves the live state AFTER the clears above -- then sc.row = sc.col = 0.
#   NOT touched by soft reset: screen contents, scrollback, live cursor position, TAB STOPS (TabReset
#     is full-only), mouse modes, alt-screen selection, title modes, bracketed paste, do_wrap
#     (pending wrap) on the live cursor, last printed char for REP is cleared only because the
#     parser is restarted (longjmp -> init_parser: lastchar = -1).
#
# DEC Table 5-9 vs xterm (the two disagree in exactly one place)
#   DECAWM   DEC: "No autowrap"          xterm/WezTerm/tessera brief: ON (resource default)   -> follow xterm
#   others agree: DECTCEM on, IRM replace, DECOM absolute, DECNRCM multinational, KAM unlocked,
#   DECNKM numeric, DECCKM normal, DECSTBM full, charsets default, SGR normal, DECSCA normal,
#   DECSC = home, DECSASD main, DECRLM LTR.
#
# DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD (recommended option first)
#   D-WRAP   Pending-wrap flag. The brief ("pending wrap cleared") contradicts xterm: soft path never
#            assigns screen->do_wrap, so a pending wrap SURVIVES DECSTR in xterm, kitty (cursor x kept)
#            and WezTerm (wrap_next untouched). Recommend KEEP (rows WRAP01/WRAP02). The *saved*
#            cursor is a different matter, see D-SAVEDWRAP.
#   D-SAVEDWRAP  xterm's CursorSave2 stores wrap_flag = live do_wrap, so DECSTR while a wrap is pending
#            leaves a saved cursor at (0,0) WITH wrap pending: a following DECRC then wraps the next
#            glyph to row 1. Clearly an xterm accident (DEC: "Home position"). Recommend saved
#            pending_wrap = false (row SAVED03, flags xterm-quirk). kitty/WezTerm invalidate the saved
#            cursor entirely; DECRC then homes and resets the pen: same observable result.
#   D-ATTRS  xterm only clears BOLD BLINK UNDERLINE INVERSE INVISIBLE + italic + colours. It does NOT
#            clear ATR_FAINT (SGR 2), ATR_STRIKEOUT (9), ATR_DBL_UNDER (21): they survive DECSTR in
#            xterm (resetRendition() would clear them but ReallyReset does not call it). DEC says
#            "Normal rendition"; kitty and WezTerm reset the whole pen. Issue #80 says "all attribute
#            flags". Recommend reset EVERYTHING (Style::DEFAULT) and note the xterm bug (row PEN03).
#            Underline colour/shape (SGR 58, 4:3) do not exist in xterm; kitty/WezTerm reset them.
#   D-PARAMS `CSI 5 ! p`: xterm's parse table dispatches CSI_EXC 'p' to CASE_DECSTR without reading
#            params, so it resets. kitty rejects it ("DECSTR escape code with parameters is invalid").
#            Recommend xterm (reset regardless of params), rows INTER03 and INTER04.
#   D-TABS   Tab stops: xterm and WezTerm keep them; kitty RESETS them (init_tabstops). Follow xterm
#            (matches the brief), row TAB01.
#   D-DECSCL xterm's DECSCL (`CSI 61..64 ; Ps " p`) is itself a soft reset (ReallyReset(soft) +
#            level change). The brief says `CSI " p` is "traced, no effect": true for the
#            parameterless form tested here (param 0 is not 61..64 so xterm does nothing either),
#            but `CSI 62 " p` is NOT a no-op in xterm. Out of scope; recommend a follow-up issue.
#   D-ALT    xterm CursorSave stores into sc[whichBuf] only (current screen's saved cursor); WezTerm
#            resets both screens', kitty both savepoints. tessera follows xterm: Grid::reset_saved_cursor
#            resets only the active screen's slot (#80). Keep that when the alternate screen becomes
#            reachable (#8); resetting both would follow WezTerm, not the oracle.
#
# ISSUE-TEXT ERRORS
#   * "the state xterm's ctlseqs lists for it": ctlseqs lists nothing; the list lives in charproc.c
#     ReallyReset and in DEC Table 5-9 (see above).
#   * "autowrap on": correct for xterm, but DEC's own table says OFF; say so in the docs.
#   * brief Done-when "pending wrap cleared": wrong vs xterm (D-WRAP). "scrollback unchanged",
#     "cursor position unchanged", "tab stops unchanged" are right.
#   * brief "keypad/cursor-key modes": tessera-term has no DECCKM/DECKPAM state (KeyboardModes in
#     keyboard.rs is a free-standing encoder argument, not Terminal state); kitty also zeroes
#     kitty key-encoding flags, xterm resets modifyOtherKeys. Only relevant once Terminal owns
#     KeyboardModes; add to the "#8: reset here" marker list.
#
# NOT TESTABLE YET (marker list for soft_reset; `// #8: reset here`)
#   DECOM off [XT bitclr ORIGIN; DEC 5-9]      DECTCEM on [XT cursor_set=ON]   DECNRCM / G0-G3 / GL / GR
#   default [XT resetCharsets]                 DECCKM off, DECKPAM off [XT]    KAM unlocked [XT]
#   DECSCA normal [XT bitclr PROTECTED]        DECLRMM off + left/right margins reset [XT resetMarginMode]
#   reverse-wraparound (?45) := default [XT]   modifyOtherKeys := default [XT]; kitty key flags [KT]
# =============================================================================


### PEN01_all_sgr_state_reset
size: 3x10
step: feed \x1b[1;4:3;31;48;2;1;2;3;58:2::9;9;9m
step: feed \x1b[!p
step: feed A
cite: [XT] ReallyReset soft: bitclr(BOLD|UNDERLINE...), reset_SGR_Colors; [DEC] Table 5-9 "SGR: Normal rendition"; brief done-list item 1 (string verbatim)
note: Bold, curly underline, strikeout, red fg and truecolor bg all gone. A is printed after the reset and must carry Style::DEFAULT; the pen itself must be DEFAULT too. The underline colour is covered by PEN06.
correction: (implementer, #80) the note claimed this string sets underline colour rgb(9,9,9). It does not: `58:2::9` carries only three sub-parameters, so the colour is dropped (ADR 0013), and the `;9;9` that follow are two SGR 9 (strikeout). Kept verbatim because the brief names it; PEN06 adds the all-colon form.
screen:
>A |
>
>
cursor: (0,1)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
pen: default
cellpen: (0,0)=default

note: Proves the SGR string sets a non-default pen (A must NOT be Style::DEFAULT: bold, curly underline, strikeout, fg indexed 1, bg rgb(1,2,3); tests/decstr.rs checks each field).
correction: (implementer, #80) the note listed underline colour rgb(9,9,9) instead of strikeout; see PEN01.
screen:
>A |
>
>
cursor: (0,1)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
pen: not default

### AWM01_autowrap_restored_on
size: 2x5
step: set auto_wrap false
step: feed abcdefg
step: feed \x1b[!p
step: feed XY
cite: [XT] ReallyReset soft bitcpy(flags, initflags, WRAPAROUND) (autoWrap resource default True); [WZ] dec_auto_wrap = true; [DEC] Table 5-9 says NO autowrap (decision: xterm)
note: With wrap off "abcdefg" ends as "abcdg" with the cursor on (0,4) and a wrap pending: xterm arms do_wrap on the last column whatever DECAWM says (print_c0_spec.txt B01). DECSTR keeps that pending wrap (WRAP01) and turns wrap on, so X wraps to row 1 and Y follows it; the first row is soft-wrapped. With wrap still off X and Y would overwrite col 4 (AWM02). Cursor does not move at DECSTR time.
correction: (implementer, #80) hand-derived row expected no pending wrap after "abcdefg" and had X on (0,4), Y on (1,0), cursor (1,1); corrected to xterm's do_wrap rule (print_c0_spec.txt B01/B02).
screen:
>abcdg\
>XY |
cursor: (1,2)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0

step: feed abcdefgXY

cite: DECAWM reset, ctlseqs CSI ? 7 l
note: Without DECSTR the last column is overwritten: "abcdY", nothing on row 1. The wrap stays pending on the last column (print_c0_spec.txt B02).
correction: (implementer, #80) pending_wrap was false; xterm arms do_wrap with DECAWM off too.
screen:
>abcdY|
>
cursor: (0,4)
pending_wrap: true
requests: []
scrollback: len=0

### REGION01_scroll_region_full
size: 6x4
step: feed \x1b[1;1Ha\x1b[2;1Hb\x1b[3;1Hc\x1b[4;1Hd\x1b[5;1He\x1b[6;1Hf
step: feed \x1b[2;4r
step: feed \x1b[!p
step: feed \x1b[6;1H\n
cite: [XT] resetMarginMode(): resetMargins() sets top/bottom to the full screen; [DEC] Table 5-9 DECSTBM top=1 bottom=page length
note: After DECSTR the region is the full screen, so LF on the last row scrolls the whole screen and 'a' moves to scrollback. If the region 2..4 survived, LF on row 6 (below the region) would do nothing (REGION02). grid.scroll_region() must equal full (0..=5).
screen:
>b
>c
>d
>e
>f
> |
cursor: (5,0)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=1 first=("a", wrapped=false)
region: full

### SAVED03_saved_pending_wrap_cleared

note: Recommended: DECRC after DECSTR gives cursor (0,0) with pending wrap FALSE, so Z overwrites 'a'. Real xterm would restore pending=true and Z would wrap to row 1 col 0 (row 0 stays "abcde", Z on row 1). The live pending wrap at DECSTR time is kept (WRAP01) but the saved copy is cleared.

### TAB01_custom_tab_stops_kept
size: 2x20

cite: [XT] TabReset is called only in the `full` (RIS) branch of ReallyReset; [WZ] no tab handling in SoftReset. [KT] differs: init_tabstops() in do_screen_reset (kitty resets stops on DECSTR). D-TABS
note: TBC 3 clears all stops, HTS sets one at col 5 only. After DECSTR, HT goes to col 5 (kept). Default stops would put X at col 8.

>

### TAB02_cleared_tab_stops_stay_cleared
size: 2x20
step: feed \x1b[3g
step: feed \x1b[!p
step: feed \tX
cite: [XT] as TAB01
note: With every stop cleared HT runs to the last column (19); X lands there and arms pending wrap. DECSTR must not restore the 8-column defaults (that would put X at col 8).
screen:
>                   X|
>
cursor: (0,19)
pending_wrap: true

### INTER01_other_intermediates_ignored_pen
size: 2x10
step: feed \x1b[31m
step: feed \x1b[?p\x1b["p\x1b[!!p\x1b[$p\x1b[? 1$p\x1b[!q\x1b[!s
step: feed A
flags: negative
cite: [XT] the parse table sends CSI ? p, CSI " p, CSI $ p to different cases (DECSCL needs params 61..64; DECRQM CSI $ p replies), `CSI ! !` is not a defined sequence
note: None of these may reach soft_reset; parser facts: `?` arrives as intermediate [63]; `"` [34]; `!!` [33,33]; `$` [36]. `CSI ! q` and `CSI ! s` carry the DECSTR intermediate with another final and must not reset either (added by the implementer, #80, after critique). A stays RED (fg indexed 1). (xterm answers `CSI $ p`/`CSI ? 1 $ p` with DECRQM replies; tessera ignores them today, not part of #80.)
screen:
>A |
>
cursor: (0,1)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
cellpen: (0,0)=fg=indexed(1)

### INTERRUPT01_can_aborts_decstr
size: 2x10
step: feed \x1b[31m
step: feed \x1b[!\x18p
step: feed A
flags: negative
cite: ECMA-48 / vt100.net state machine: CAN (0x18) cancels the sequence; the final byte `p` then prints as text (csi_spec.txt parser facts)
note: No reset: pen stays red and a literal 'p' is printed before A.
screen:
>pA |
>
cursor: (0,2)
pending_wrap: false
requests: []
scrollback: len=0
cellpen: (0,1)=fg=indexed(1)

# -- end of cases

#> Rows to add when #8 lands (state does not exist in tessera-term yet; sources in the header list):
#>   DECOM on + CUP, DECSTR, CUP 1;1 -> absolute (cursor (0,0) not region-relative)     [XT bitclr ORIGIN]
#>   DECSET ?25 l (hide cursor), DECSTR -> visible                                        [XT cursor_set=ON; DEC DECTCEM]
#>   SCS "ESC ( 0" (line drawing) + SO, DECSTR, print 'q' -> literal 'q'                  [XT resetCharsets]
#>   DECCKM set, DECSTR -> normal cursor keys; DECKPAM set, DECSTR -> numeric keypad      [XT keyboard.flags]
#>   DECSTR with DECOM on and DECSC saved -> DECRC lands at (0,0) with origin off          [XT bitclr ORIGIN before CursorSave]
#>   DECLRMM on + DECSLRM, DECSTR -> left/right margins full, mode off                     [XT resetMarginMode]
#> Rows to add with the state they need (not #8; found by the #80 adversarial run):
#>   DECSCUSR `CSI 4 SP q` (steady underline), DECSTR -> default cursor shape and blink    [XT ReallyReset soft; no issue yet]
#>   OSC 4 ; 1 ; rgb:00/ff/00 (palette 1 = green), DECSTR -> palette 1 back to the theme   [XT ResetAnsiColorRequest; #9]
